description: Registry of every agent definition in a declared scope, the provider surface(s) that expose it, and the relationship between those surfaces. A provider directory is NOT canonical merely because a provider loads it: canonical routing identity lives here, prompt bodies live on the surfaces. Edit here -- scripts/check-agent-registry.py fails if this file and the trees disagree in either direction.

agent_pack.loaded_by: The icn-agent-pack Claude Code plugin (tools/claude-code/plugins/icn-agent-pack/.claude-plugin/plugin.json), loaded when a developer installs the plugin. Its README states it complements rather than replaces the project-local .claude/ config, so an agent name here can coexist with a different body under .claude/agents.

copilot.loaded_by: GitHub Copilot custom agents. Routed by .github/copilot-instructions.md; .github/agents/README.md documents the surface. NOTE: this field deliberately makes NO claim about which agents are automatically invocable. An earlier revision summarised that here and the summary was wrong -- it said every agent but icn-orchestrator declared infer: false, while icn-docs-synchronizer declares neither invocation key and is therefore automatically invocable. Nothing validated the prose. Per-agent automatic_invocation is the mechanically enforced answer; do not restate it here.

mirror_pairs_note: A record may additionally name mirror_pairs: surface pairs whose bodies MUST stay byte-identical, enforced by the checker even when the record as a whole is divergent. This exists because .github/copilot-instructions.md states that icn-code-reviewer 'mirrors its Claude counterpart' -- a claim that was documented and unenforced. A record-level relationship cannot express it once a third surface diverges.

relationship_model.single_surface: Exposed by exactly one provider. No cross-surface claim is made.
relationship_model.exact_mirror: Exposed by every named surface with byte-identical bodies modulo provider front matter. MECHANICALLY ENFORCED: the checker re-compares the bodies, so a mirror that drifts fails rather than silently becoming a variant.
relationship_model.provider_variant: Exposed by both providers with deliberately different bodies. Requires divergence.adjudicated = true and a why. Not enforced byte-wise, by definition.
relationship_model.divergent_unreviewed: Exposed by both providers with different bodies whose intent has NOT been adjudicated. Requires divergence.owning_issue. This value exists so an unreviewed divergence is explicit debt rather than two unrelated definitions silently sharing one name.

out_of_scope: Agent directories outside the repository -- for example a project-level ~/.claude/agents/ -- are machine-local. They are neither registered nor enforceable here. The icn-agents/v1 'orchestrator' record pointed at ../../../.claude/agents/orchestrator.md, which escapes the repository root; it named no in-repo file and no checker covered it, so it never failed. Removed rather than repointed: see the note on icn-orchestrator below.
.github/agents/README.md documents the Copilot surface and is not an agent definition. The same applies to any README.md in a surface tree.

`.codex/skills/*/agents/` directories exist but hold no agent definitions today. They sit inside skill trees owned by ops/state/truth/skills.json#enforcement.scan_scope, so they are that registry's territory, not this one's. If an agent definition ever lands there it must be declared as a surface here rather than absorbed silently.

Prompt CONTENT is out of scope here: this registry owns inventory and provider topology. An earlier revision said stale doctrine 'is enforced by forbidden_patterns'. That was FALSE and gave a false assurance. The only forbidden_patterns implementation is scripts/check-skill-registry.py, and skills.json#enforcement.scan_scope covers ops/automation/skills, .agents/skills and .claude/skills -- ZERO overlap with the three agent trees registered here. Prompt content on these surfaces is therefore enforced by NOTHING today, and known stale doctrine remains reachable, including a DID form the code rejects sitting behind an automatically invocable Copilot router. Closing that gap is icn#2632 STAGE 2, which must clean the existing violations and extend scan_scope in one tranche -- adding dirty trees to scan scope first would only turn a silent gap into a red gate. This file states the gap; it does not gate it.

The registry does not describe its own enforcement. An earlier revision carried an `enforcement` block naming the checker, its tests and its callers; nothing outside the checker ever dereferenced it, and four review rounds went into machinery proving a self-description no consumer needed. The gates are real and unchanged -- ops/scripts/drift-check.sh, scripts/check-preflight-consistency.sh and .github/workflows/agent-drift-check.yml each invoke the checker directly -- they simply do not need their identities copied into the agent-routing registry to do it.
declared_scope.completeness_claim: Across every surface declared in provider_surfaces, every provider-loaded agent definition is represented exactly once, and every registered path maps back to a real provider definition. provider_surfaces is the ONE machine-readable owner of provider topology: an earlier revision also listed the in-scope globs here, which nothing read -- inventory is driven by provider_surfaces[].tree and the direct-child *.md convention -- so a glob added to that list changed no behaviour while making this claim false. scripts/check-agent-registry.py fails if either direction breaks.

supported_input_domain.note: The exact inputs scripts/check-agent-registry.py claims to decide correctly, and the ownership boundary it decides them under. Written down so a review finding can be classified rather than argued: a counterexample INSIDE this domain that the checker gets wrong is a defect; one outside it is a documented limitation. Derived from what the repository actually contains, what the implementation intentionally supports, and the provider conventions we claim to honour -- not from what is convenient to exclude. Adopted icn#2632 after ten consecutive review rounds in one defect class established that an unwritten domain cannot terminate a review.

ownership.yaml_parse_validity: A real YAML parser (PyYAML). The checker does not decide whether front matter is valid YAML and must never reimplement that. If ICN accepts a definition, a parser accepts it; the converse deliberately does not hold.
ownership.duplicate_top_level_keys: ICN, explicitly. A YAML loader accepts a repeated key and silently keeps the last value; ICN refuses the ambiguity outright, because a routing or capability field certified as whichever value a loader happened to keep is not a certified field.
ownership.icn_registry_schema: ICN. Root, record, surface-declaration and divergence vocabularies are CLOSED allowlists. An unrecognised key fails: it is most often a misspelling, which otherwise drops its meaning silently.
ownership.provider_surface_relationships: ICN. single_surface, exact_mirror, provider_variant and divergent_unreviewed, plus mirror_pairs, with the declared and implemented vocabularies required equal in both directions.
ownership.logical_name_derivation: ICN, provider-aware. github-copilot definitions may be spelled <name>.md or <name>.agent.md -- GitHub's configuration reference takes the file name 'minus .md or .agent.md'. claude-code has no .agent.md convention, so there the suffix is part of the name.
ownership.reachable_agent_routing: ICN. routing_triggers must be nonempty: this file is the canonical owner of agent routing, and an empty list is the absence of a routing record wearing the shape of a satisfied field. not_for may be empty -- excluding nothing is an answer.
ownership.filesystem_and_truth_owner_accessibility: ICN, fail-closed. A repository-controlled path is untrusted input: a directory named like a definition, a non-UTF-8 file, an unreadable truth owner, a symlink escaping the tree and a symlink cycle must each produce a FINDING. A checker that crashes reports nothing, and nothing reads as clean.
ownership.provider_native_syntax: The provider definition. description, color, model, tools, target, mcp-servers, metadata, infer, disable-model-invocation and user-invocable are never copied here; the registry records derived SEMANTICS. A provider-owned key at any level of this document is refused.

supported_front_matter: A `---` delimited block whose root mapping begins at column 0.

Plain unquoted top-level keys. Quoted, explicit (`? key`), flow-mapping and space-before-colon spellings are valid YAML and are refused, because the line-based semantic readers would treat them as absent.

Values ICN CONSUMES (name, description, infer, disable-model-invocation, and provider-required fields) must be read identically by the line reader and by the parser. A value the two disagree about is refused rather than guessed at.
Values ICN does not consume are the provider's business: booleans, numbers, flow collections and multi-line forms are all accepted so long as the document parses.

required_execution_surfaces.note: Required check `Agent Tooling Drift Check`. Provisions the dependency and runs the checker.
Documented as runnable standalone; runs the checker, so it needs the dependency locally.
Same: runs the checker as part of preflight.
Run directly by contributors and by the invariants suite.

supported_input_domain.dependency_contract: PyYAML is REQUIRED, declared in scripts/requirements.txt, installed by the workflow from that file, and its absence exits 1 with instructions rather than skipping the check. A correctness check that silently disappears reports the skip as a pass. Every authoritative description of the scripts/ surface -- including the generated agent context spine -- must say so.
explicitly_out_of_contract: Deciding what a valid-YAML document MEANS beyond the keys listed above. Front matter ICN does not consume is the provider's contract, not this one's.
Repairing or normalising malformed input. Every unsupported form fails explicitly; nothing is interpreted as absence, default, or harmlessness.
Provider behaviour beyond the semantic projections declared in provider_metadata_ownership.
Agent directories outside the repository, which are machine-local and unenforceable -- see out_of_scope above.

divergence.evidence: Pairwise body similarity is NOT stored. It is derived data that a partial prompt edit makes stale while the record still reads green, so storing it recreates the defect this registry exists to end. scripts/check-agent-registry.py --verbose recomputes and prints it fresh on every run.

provider_metadata_ownership.principle: The registry owns logical identity, surface topology, relationships, and semantic projections that are organizationally meaningful. A provider definition owns its own native syntax. The translation between them is owned by scripts/check-agent-registry.py, so the shape is provider syntax -> provider adapter -> stable registry claim, never provider syntax <-> duplicated provider syntax. A value appears in both places only when the checker pins the registry's claim: an enforced projection is not a second owner; an unenforced copy is.

owned_here.surfaces.<surface>.automatic_invocation: Can this provider surface cause the agent to be selected WITHOUT an explicit invocation? That question is organizationally meaningful -- it is the difference between an agent that influences ICN work on request and one that can influence it unbidden, which is the population this registry exists to enumerate. It is a SEMANTIC projection, not a provider key: the previous revision stored Copilot's raw `infer`, which GitHub has since retired, so the registry was pinned to obsolete syntax. Derived per surface by the checker's adapter and re-derived on every run.
owned_here.derivation.copilot: disable-model-invocation when present (inverted), else the retired `infer`, else true. Verified against https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/custom-agents-configuration on 2026-08-30: `infer` is RETIRED with default true; `disable-model-invocation` replaces it, defaults to false, and takes precedence when both are present. An agent declaring neither key IS automatically invocable -- recording that absence as unknown would be truthful about syntax and false about behaviour.

owned_by_the_provider.description / color / model / tools / ta: Provider-native. No consumer read them from the registry -- verified across every agents.json reader -- so 71 copies were removed and the checker now rejects them coming back.
owned_by_the_provider.infer / disable-model-invocation / user-: Provider SYNTAX. The registry records the derived automatic_invocation semantic instead, so a provider renaming its key does not change the registry's concept. Recording the raw keys is rejected.
owned_by_the_provider.provider_front_matter_keys (removed): This surface field listed each provider's front-matter keys and had ZERO consumers -- verified across the branch. It had already rotted: the copilot surface still listed `infer`, the key GitHub retired and this registry stopped modelling. Removed rather than synchronised, per the rule this file now follows.

deliberately_not_projected.user-invocable: GitHub documents it (default true) and it would project cleanly as manual_invocation. NOT added: no ICN consumer or invariant needs to answer 'can a person pick this agent by hand', and the registry must not grow a projection merely because the provider supports the field. Add it when a real consumer appears, not before.

provider_metadata_ownership.registry_native: name, surfaces, relationship, mirror_pairs, divergence, routing_triggers and not_for exist only here. They are cross-provider routing intent and topology, so no provider file is their source and nothing needs pinning.

provider_type_note: provider_type names the provider TECHNOLOGY and is what semantic adapters dispatch on. The surface key beside it ('claude', 'copilot', 'agent_pack') is an arbitrary logical label and carries no behaviour: renaming it must not change enforcement. Two surfaces may share a provider_type -- .claude/agents and the icn-agent-pack plugin tree are both loaded by Claude Code -- and a provider_type with no adapter in scripts/check-agent-registry.py#PROVIDER_ADAPTERS fails rather than silently projecting nothing. A type that genuinely projects no organizational behaviour maps to an explicit empty adapter, so 'projects nothing' is a decision rather than an omission.
